correctness.rationale: Exact coordinate reduction gives N^2=u^2+v^2 on |u|>=|v| and N^2=2v^2 on |v|>=|u|. Averaging any positive-definite Euclidean pullback with the coordinate-swap isometry preserves its two-sided comparison constants and diagonalizes it in (u,v), reducing the global problem to q_t=u^2+t v^2. The exact ratio extrema are {1,t/2,(1+t)/2}; their piecewise quotient is minimized at t=2 with value 3/2. An explicit vector pair gives C_NJ>=3/2, while Euclidean pullback comparison gives C_NJ<=d_BM^2=3/2. Boundaries and quantifiers are included; no computation substitutes for proof.
